data.raw_text:
Drone footage on Wednesday, Nov. 12 showed vast areas of Taiwan’s largely rural eastern county of Yilan inundated after Typhoon Fun-wong brought excessive downpours ahead of its expected landfall.

Reuters was able to independently verify the location of the video through the road layout, bridge and buildings, which matched file and satellite images. Reuters was able to verify the date of the footage from the original file metadata.

The island’s fire department said about 8,300 people were moved from their homes to safer areas, mostly in Yilan and nearby Hualien, where a monsoon from the north swelled the rainfall with the unseasonably late typhoon.

Fung-wong is forecast to graze the far southern tip of Taiwan later on Wednesday before heading into the Pacific Ocean. It lost considerable strength after swirling through the Philippines to kill 27 people.

Courtesy: OMER PHOTOGRAPHY via Reuters

data.raw_text:
A much weakened Typhoon Fung-wong approached southern Taiwan on Wednesday, November 12, as it brought heavy downpours to the mountainous east coast and unleashed floods that ran neck-high in places.

Fung-wong is forecast to graze the far southern tip of Taiwan later on Wednesday before heading into the Pacific Ocean. It lost considerable strength after swirling through the Philippines to kill 27 people.

In Taiwan, the fire department said about 8,300 people were moved from their homes to safer areas, mostly in Yilan and nearby Hualien, where a monsoon from the north swelled the rainfall with the unseasonably late typhoon. Businesses and schools were shut in most southern areas of the island, with 51 people injured.

Courtesy: https://t.co/MM9RtNJDth via Reuters
